subject: Regional resilience scope / boundary exception request
messages:
From: Elena Morris <elena.morris@greenlightpay.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@greenlightpay.com, eng-team@greenlightpay.com
Date: 2025-09-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Question on multi-region RTO/RPO and carveout options

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the demo last week — the latency profiles looked promising. Before we move this through procurement, the security team has one sticking point around cross-region failover. Our core payment flows are required by our regulators to have a documented RTO of 15 minutes and RPO of no data loss across regions.

Given our architecture and the fact that we will be running a custom caching layer, we wanted to check whether Redwood can commit to 15m RTO / zero RPO across two independent regions (us-west2 / us-east1) or whether there is an exception path for a staged warm-standby approach with documented activation lead time and data-sync expectations.

If you have a standard carveout template we can review (or a recent example), that would help us avoid lengthy legal redlines.

Also: can you surface any metrics or historical failover timelines for similar fintech customers?

Appreciate it —
Elena
Senior Security Program Manager
GreenLight Pay

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: Elena Morris <elena.morris@greenlightpay.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2025-09-12T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on multi-region RTO/RPO and carveout options

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the clear summary. Short answer: our standard fully-managed hosted offering provides cross-region failover but the hard guarantee you cite (15m / zero-RPO) is not typical for multi-region failover without additional reserved capacity and an architecture-level data replication agreement. We do have a documented exception path for customers with regulated requirements that combines warm-standby topologies, write-through caching, and an activation SLA.

I'll pull a redline-friendly amendment and a short matrix showing trade-offs between RTO, RPO, and cost. Kar (cc) will own the procurement/contract touchpoints, and Laura can confirm the engineering feasibility and operational caveats.

Proposed next steps:
- We will send a draft SLA amendment and a one-page failover matrix by EOD tomorrow.
- Internal review with your security lead: can you share a preferred window for a 30–45 minute call tomorrow?

Attaching a brief checklist (high level) in the follow-up.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, Elena Morris <elena.morris@greenlightpay.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2025-09-12T13:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on multi-region RTO/RPO and carveout options

Hi Elena and team —

Adding a procurement perspective: there are two pragmatic commercial approaches we typically discuss for this class of request:

1) Reserved dual-region capacity + active-active replication support: higher monthly commitment, enables tighter failover windows because we pre-warm capacity in both regions.
2) Warm-standby with activation SLA and reimbursable capacity ramp: lower monthly base, with a documented activation lead time (we model 15–60 minutes depending on state sync) and an agreed credit band if activation exceeds SLA.

For regulated customers we often sign a short addendum that specifies activation triggers, notification procedures, and a limited liability profile for the carveout period. I will include sample wording in the draft SLA amendment.

Quick ask: Is there an internal maximum monthly commit GreenLight is willing to consider for dual-region reserved capacity? That will guide whether we recommend approach (1) or (2).

—Karthik
Commercial Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Elena Morris <elena.morris@greenlightpay.com>, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2025-09-13T08:09:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on multi-region RTO/RPO and carveout options

Hi Elena —

Attaching a technical matrix (see attachment stub) that maps topology -> typical RTO -> typical RPO -> operational caveats. High-level bullets:
- Active-active with synchronous replication (rare for our stack) can approach sub-15m RTO and near-zero RPO but requires customer-managed synchronous datastore and higher network SLA between regions.
- Active-passive with pre-warmed capacity in standby region (our common pattern) gives predictable activation but RTO is driven by state transfer; we typically model 15–45m if KV cache is small, 30–120m for large working sets unless you adopt write-through replication.
- Warm-standby (cold KV) will have RTO >2 hours in worst cases unless we implement streaming replication and application-level replay.

Operational caveats to include in an amendment:
- Precise RTO/RPO windows tied to customer-controlled replication cadence and KV cache size.
- Activation procedure: paging, verification, cutover, and rollback windows.
- Testing cadence: annual failover runbooks and quarterly tabletop exercises required for exception to remain in force.

I've also included a redlineable amendment draft (sla_amendment_draft.docx stub) with sample language for credits, activation metrics, and required test plans. Happy to walk through it on a call.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Principal Reliability Engineer (Redwood Runtime)

[Attachment: redwood_failover_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB) — matrix of topologies and measured activation times]
[Attachment: sla_amendment_draft.docx (docx, 18KB) — draft amendment with credit bands]

From: Elena Morris <elena.morris@greenlightpay.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@greenlightpay.com
Date: 2025-09-14T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on multi-region RTO/RPO and carveout options

Thanks, Laura and team — this is helpful. Procurement and security reviewed the draft and proposed the following:

- GreenLight can accept a warm-standby approach for non-critical analytic replication, but for the payment authorization path we require an operational path to 15m RTO and zero RPO for a cardinal subset of transactions.
- We propose a hybrid carveout: Redwood implements a pre-warmed dedicated pool in standby region for the authorization path (commit monthly), while non-critical routes remain warm-standby with the standard activation SLA.

We can commit to a 12-month reserved spend for the dedicated pool if we can agree on an activation SLA of 15m (target) / 30m (p75) with a credit schedule if breached. We also require a quarterly failover test and a runbook shared at least 2 weeks before each test.

If Redwood is comfortable with that framing we will push procurement to sign quickly.

Elena

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: Elena Morris <elena.morris@greenlightpay.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, procurement@greenlightpay.com
Date: 2025-09-15T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on multi-region RTO/RPO and carveout options

Elena —

This is a workable framing and matches a pattern we've implemented for other regulated payments customers. Next steps from Redwood:

1) I will circulate a redlined SLA amendment today that encodes the hybrid carveout (dedicated standby pool for authorization path + warm-standby for non-critical routes), the activation SLA band (15m target / 30m p75), and the quarterly test cadence.
2) Kar will include a pricing sheet for a 12-month reserved pool with an optional stepdown after 9 months tied to observed failover metrics.
3) Laura will draft a simplified runbook template for your security team to use in quarterly tests.

We'll link the DocuSign envelope to the shared drive once the amendment is redlined; providing the test window is acceptable, we should be able to get this to legal/ops signatures in 7–10 business days.

Thanks — will follow up with attachments and the Docusign link.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
